before.reasoning: Lungo-Koehn signed the City Climate Change Commitment and committed Medford to 100% renewable electricity for city operations by 2030 and net-zero emissions citywide by 2050. She participated in the Metro Mayors Coalition climate working group and publicly stated that climate change is an existential threat requiring urgent local action. She has backed state climate legislation including the 2021 MA Climate Act and directed city buildings to transition away from fossil fuel heating.

rows.why: BOTH citations were unreachable — metromayor.org has no DNS and no captures, and medfordma.org/departments/sustainability/climate-action/ returns 404 (as does its parent; the root is 200, so the site reorganised). Chair 1 is 'declare a climate emergency and ban all activities that increase carbon emissions'; Medford declared no emergency and banned nothing. The old reasoning also overstated the 2030 target as '100% renewable electricity' when the actual commitment is a 50% cut, and named a 'City Climate Change Commitment' document that does not exist. Its Metro Mayors clause was TRUE — only the host cited for it died.

before.reasoning: Mejia has used the Controller's office to audit city sustainability spending and track progress on climate commitments. He has published transparency reports on how climate and environmental funds are spent across city departments, holding the city accountable to its climate goals.

rows.why: Cited a dead host (kennethforla.com, zero captures) and a bare root (lacontroller.org; his official site is controller.lacity.gov). More seriously, the old reasoning described his JOB, not a position — auditing sustainability spending is compatible with any chair, so the row was scored 2 on evidence that could not distinguish 2 from 4. Real evidence exists and is now cited: he wants Los Angeles at 100% clean, renewable energy by 2030. Right chair, wrong basis.
